name: Evil-Merodach
title: King of Babylon who released Jehoiachin
summary: Evil-Merodach (also known as Amel-Marduk) was the son of Nebuchadnezzar and king of Babylon from about 562 to 560 BC. He is known in the Bible for releasing Jehoiachin, the king of Judah, from prison after 37 years of captivity and giving him a place of honor at his table. This act was seen as a glimmer of hope for the Jewish people during their exile.

keyEvents.title: Release of Jehoiachin from Prison
keyEvents.description: In the year Evil-Merodach became king over Babylon, he released Jehoiachin, the king of Judah, from prison after 37 years of captivity.

keyEvents.title: Evil-Merodach spoke kindly to Jehoiachin
keyEvents.description: Evil-Merodach showed kindness to Jehoiachin and spoke kindly to him, marking a change in how the captive king was treated.

keyEvents.title: Jehoiachin Given Honor Above Other Kings
keyEvents.description: Evil-Merodach placed Jehoiachin's throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon, giving him a prominent position.

keyEvents.title: Jehoiachin's Prison Clothes Were Replaced
keyEvents.description: Jehoiachin was allowed to take off his prison clothes and eat at the king's table for the rest of his life, as a sign of restored dignity.

keyEvents.title: Regular allowance for Jehoiachin
keyEvents.description: Evil-merodach gave Jehoiachin a regular daily allowance all the days of his life, which secured his livelihood in exile.
